sb.lingua_aiuto: Language of the interface and of the command-line messages. Your choice is remembered.
sb.congelata: Settings are locked while a job is running: the queue keeps the parameters it started with. They unlock when the queue finishes (or is stopped).
sb.valgono: These apply to every file. The model is chosen per file in the Processing tab.
sb.altezza_aiuto: The width follows the real aspect ratio, with square pixels: 4:3 stays 4:3 and anamorphic video isn't squashed.
sb.crf_aiuto: Lower = higher quality and a bigger file. At 18 the measured difference from lossless is 54 dB: imperceptible.
sb.preset_aiuto: Slower = smaller file at the same quality. It affects encoding, not the upscale.
sb.avanzate_nota: The defaults are right almost every time.
sb.dedup_aiuto: Skips the identical frames of animation drawn "on twos": on the footage tested it halved processing time. Checked on every chunk: if a frame with real motion were dropped, it gets processed again.
sb.denoise_aiuto: Only useful on noisy sources: the model would amplify compression noise along with the artwork.
sb.forza_aiuto: Normally AnimeUp refuses upscales smaller than 1.25x: they cost the same hours for very few extra pixels.
sb.approf_aiuto: Measures the deduplication of every source instead of estimating it from previously processed files, for more accurate time estimates. It takes roughly 11 seconds for a 360p file, 40 seconds for 720p and 69 seconds for 1080p, once per file. When this is off, you can still request the measurement for individual files.
sb.disco_ridotto: The space you set ({ora} GB) is no longer available on this disk: {libero} GB free. Lowered to {tetto} GB, which leaves enough room for the system.
sb.disco_aiuto: How much disk ONE file may use while it's being processed: extracted frames, chunks and segments together. Higher = fewer chunks and a few minutes saved. The minimum depends on duration and resolution, and you're told before starting if it isn't enough. It's a cap, not a reservation: a file only takes what it needs. The default is the more cautious of 85% of free space and "everything minus 40 GB".
sb.pausa_aiuto: Minutes of rest between one file and the next, to give the CPU and GPU a break during long runs. During the pause Start stays disabled and the bar shows when work resumes. 0 = no pause.
sb.taratura_aiuto: Times this Mac on the sample clip (models, extraction and encoding) and adapts every estimate to its real speed. About 10 minutes, with the GPU idle.
sb.sospeso: There's a paused file that was started with different parameters ({diversi}). Resume will still use its own parameters: changes here only apply to new jobs.
sb.ripristina: Reset the sidebar to the paused file's parameters
sb.chiudi_aiuto: Shuts down the interface (the server). Running jobs do NOT stop: they carry on by themselves and are still there next time you open AnimeUp.
sb.chiudi_avviso: The running job will NOT stop: it keeps going in the background and will be there next time you open AnimeUp. To stop everything, use "Stop all" in Processing first.
src.vuoto_testo:
Copy the files you want to process into **{cartella}**.

Whole series are fine, and resolutions may differ from file to file.
src.sottotitolo: Every file copied into INPUT is analysed automatically: resolution, timing, tracks and the warnings worth knowing before processing it. Open a row for the full report.
src.rianalizza_tutti_aiuto: Analyses every file again from scratch, ignoring saved results. Useful if files have changed but kept the same name.
src.analisi_in_corso.uno: Analysing — {n} file left. Meanwhile you can use the other tabs: files not analysed yet show up there as pending and fill in by themselves when their turn comes.
src.analisi_in_corso.altri: Analysing — {n} files to go. Meanwhile you can use the other tabs: files not analysed yet show up there as pending and fill in by themselves when their turn comes.
src.dedup_non_misurabile: dedup can't be measured on this file
src.approfondita_aiuto:
Measures deduplication directly on this file instead of inferring it from files already processed. It tells you BEFORE starting how long the job will really take: in one real case the inferred dedup said 6.5% where the true value was 33%, an estimate off by almost four hours out of thirteen.

It takes from about ten seconds (360p) to just over a minute (a 25-minute 1080p file), runs in the background and is done ONCE: the result is saved. The analysis already done isn't repeated.
src.rianalizza_aiuto: Analyses this file again from scratch, ignoring saved results.
probe.troncato: File probably truncated: the container declares {dichiarata}s but the video stops {mancano}s earlier. The output would end there.
probe.vfr: VFR source: the frame rate varies. It will be normalised during extraction, without re-encoding the source.
probe.buchi: {mancanti} frames missing ({buchi} gaps in the sequence): the rip is incomplete. Gaps will be filled by repeating the previous frame so the duration doesn't change.
probe.container_discorde: The container declares {dichiarato} fps but the timestamps say {misurato} fps. Using the measured value.
probe.fps_non_standard: Non-standard frame rate ({fps}): probably an inaccurate rip. Check the preview result.
probe.interlacciato: Interlaced content: AnimeUp doesn't deinterlace, and the model would upscale the combing lines into permanent artefacts. Prepare the file with a dedicated tool first, then put it back in INPUT.
probe.telecine: 3:2 telecine detected: the content is 23.976 inside a 29.97 container. AnimeUp doesn't do inverse telecine: recover the original frames with a dedicated tool first, then put the file back in INPUT.
probe.anamorfico: Non-square pixels (SAR {sar}): the output will be normalised to {larghezza}x{altezza} so the image isn't distorted.
probe.mov_text: mov_text subtitles: they can't be copied into MKV and will be converted to SRT.
probe.no_video: No usable video track: this file can't be processed.
probe.colore_hd: No colour metadata: BT.709 (HD source) will be assumed, as is the convention, and the tags will be written explicitly in the output.
probe.colore_sd: No colour metadata: BT.601 (SD source) will be assumed, as is the convention, and the tags will be written explicitly in the output.
